duties:
The duties include supporting and expanding MSS initiatives, with a particular focus on U(t)-Mathazine. Responsibilities include promoting this publication among students, faculty, and the broader mathematical community; strengthening connections with the Canadian Mathematical Society and other relevant organizations; recruiting, training, and coordinating volunteer editors and reviewers; and supervising and mentoring student authors throughout the writing, editing, and publication process to help them produce high-quality submissions.

Additional responsibilities include identifying opportunities to increase student participation, organizing promotional activities and outreach events, developing strategies to improve the visibility and impact of these publications, coordinating editorial workflows, and contributing ideas that enhance the quality, sustainability, and long-term growth of this initiative. The role also involves exploring new collaborations and innovative approaches to ensure that this MSS initiative continue to evolve and reach a wider audience.

Through its student-led editorial process, U(t)-Mathazine fosters a vibrant mathematical community, highlights student achievements, and makes mathematics more accessible and enjoyable to a broad audience. The publication also serves as a platform for outreach and knowledge sharing, strengthening connections within the University of Toronto and with the broader mathematical community.

Appointment Dates: September 15, 2026- August 31, 2027
Scheduled Hours: 12.5 hours per month

To complete the application, please upload:
1. Cover Letter (maximum one page) describing: Their interest in the position. Relevant experience with writing, editing, mentoring, outreach, or student leadership. Why they are interested in contributing to U(t)-Mathazine and MSS initiatives. Any ideas they have for expanding the publication's reach and increasing student engagement.
2. Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Résumé highlighting relevant academic, volunteer, employment, and leadership experience.
3. Writing Sample (1–3 pages) demonstrating clear and engaging writing. This may be an expository article, course assignment, blog post, newsletter article, or other sample of the applicant's writing.
4. Editing Sample (optional but encouraged). Applicants may submit an example of a document they have edited or proofread or briefly describe their editing experience.
5. Portfolio (optional). Applicants with experience in graphic design, website development, social media, or publication layout may include links or samples of their work.
6. Names and contact information for one or two references who can comment on the applicant's communication skills, reliability, and ability to work collaboratively.

duties:
Engineering Science Capstone Design is a 4th year Capstone design course in the Engineering Physics Program. Teams of 3-5 students undertake independent design projects centred on creating, updating or improving experiemental setups in the Advanced Physics Labs, which are used to support undergraduate teaching and learning in the Engineering Science and Physics departments. Students are responsible for proposing a new/improved/updated experiment, then working as a team to realize their design. The goal is to create a fully functional experimental setup which can be used in future offerings of the Advanced Physics Lab courses.

As the Assessment & Project Support TA, you will be expected to work together with the instructor to guide student teams' design work, in particular how to frame their chosen project using the language of engineering design learned in earlier design courses, then follow through on the plan. You will also be involved in grading written design reports created by student teams, as well as individual reflective writing. You will meet with the student teams (along with the instructor) at several critical points in the semester: before and after major deliverables are due. 

You will be expected to provide constructive, actionable feedback to students for their written deliverables, which they will use to improve for future assignments.

duties:
Studio TAs in ESC204 are responsible for leading one or two weekly design studio (tutorial and practical) sections, supporting in-lecture workshops and active learning activities, and assessing and providing feedback on student work. They must also attend regular weekly meeting(s), as well as several additional meetings (to be scheduled at the beginning of the term) related to grading assignments. To support these varied activities, course-specific training will be offered in the fall. 
 
Studios (2-hour tutorial and practical blocks consisting of approximately 24 students which meet twice weekly) mainly involve activities related to engineering design, and help students build skills around effective teamwork, project management, understanding unfamiliar design contexts and stakeholders, technical design and prototyping, and communication. For technical design and prototyping, TAs will also facilitate interactions between students and course partners such as the Myhal Fabrication Facility during studio: https://uoft.me/myfab. In addition, TAs will give feedback on and approve student orders for parts and services from the Fabrication Facility outside of studio time.  
 
Each TA is expected to support one or two studio sections. For TAs supporting one studio, there is some flexibility in which section you are assigned to accommodate your availability, but you will have to be available for both meeting times for your assigned section(s) each week. In addition to leading studio sessions, TAs will assess oral presentations (during studio) as well as (asynchronously) assessing written and other multi-media student work, including CAD models, sketches, videos and photographs of mechatronic systems, circuit diagrams, functional block diagrams, project management documentation, and other design-relevant artifacts. As part of all assessments, TAs are expected to provide constructive, actionable feedback to students to help them improve from deliverable to deliverable. 
 
All Studio TAs are also required to attend weekly course team meetings (two per week for the first six weeks, and one per week thereafter). Weekly course team meetings will include a debrief of the previous week�s studio activities, plans for the upcoming week�s studio activities, and discussion of any problems that may arise. Meetings will be held in hybrid format with in-person attendance required except by prior arrangement. In addition, you will be required to attend some lectures to assist students with hands-on teamwork and active learning activities during lecture, and/or hold "Prototyping Support Hours" in the Myhal Light Fabrication Facility to support ongoing prototyping work. 
 
TAs will be supported by faculty co-leads, an engineering communication instructor, and will work together to share duties relating to course logistics as part of a large, tight-knit TA team. 
 
Studio sessions, meetings and lectures are planned to be held in-person, unless there are changes to health policies that prevent in-person course delivery. Lectures will be recorded for accommodation reasons; however, you must plan to attend lecture in-person as needed to support active learning. Any changes to the course delivery (in-person, online, or a hybrid of both), will be communicated by the University at a later date.  
 
All TAs are required to complete all components of the Myhal Fabrication Facility Safety Training (Tier-1 and Tier-2): https://uoft.me/myfabsafety.

duties:
This new Math and Numeracy program is an in-person academic support initiative designed to help students strengthen foundational mathematics knowledge and develop effective learning strategies. The program is designed to support students who are seeking to address knowledge gaps, reflect on their learning, build confidence, and prepare for first year university calculus courses. Through interactive instruction, facilitated group work, independent exercises, and feedback, the program aims to improve student readiness, retention, and overall academic success. The program is designed to primarily support students who intend to take first-year calculus classes (MAT 132/34, 135/36).

Working collaboratively with the Learning Strategist (Math & Numeracy Focus) and the Math and Numeracy Instructor, the TA will support this new Math and Numeracy program, a 4-week in-person program which combines a review of essential mathematical concepts (e.g., algebra, trigonometry, functions) with learning strategy instruction (e.g., critical thinking, problem solving, resilience, managing test anxiety). The TA will support curriculum development, attend lessons, facilitate group work during classes, lead drop-in and review sessions, mark assessments, and provides individualized student support and feedback. The TA will foster an inclusive and supportive learning environment that promotes student engagement and community-building.

duties:
The Lawrence Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing Program provides a full-time, two-year, second entry baccalaureate nursing education. Given that nursing is a practice-based profession, we believe that clinical experience is a vital and integral component of the curriculum, providing students with hands-on opportunities to actively apply classroom learning to ‘real life’ nursing practice under the supervision and support of a clinical teacher. Clinical Instructors (CIs) play an important role in facilitating student learning to further develop students’ knowledge, skill, and judgement. CIs are required to complete all on-boarding and orientation activities required by the faculty in preparation for their clinical teaching role. Ongoing support will be provided throughout the term by Course Faculty, the Undergraduate Clinical Resource Faculty, and the Clinical Education Office.  Applicants should note that commitment to the role for the entire term is needed for consistency in the development, assessment, and evaluation of nursing students.   
Duties and Responsibilities: 
1. Complete the asynchronous CI orientation learning modules as required and attend the in-person Faculty-led CI orientation for NUR 440.  
2. Familiarize themselves with and uphold all faculty and university policies related to clinical placements (e.g., CI and Student Absences, Professional Behavior).  
3. Attend all clinical activities as scheduled. 
a.  Personal obligations (e.g. attending conferences, vacations, or appointments) are to be scheduled outside of the clinical activities. 
b.  In the case of extenuating circumstances (e.g. illness and/or bereavement) – CIs are required to notify the Clinical Education Office with the dates as soon as possible. CIs may also be asked to assist the Clinical Education Office to arrange for a possible replacement instructor. 
4. Assist students to create clinical learning objectives for their respective clinical activities that are reflective of course outcomes, clinical practice expectations, and students’ level of learning.  
5. Encourage an inquiring, theory, and evidence-based approach to nursing practice. 
6. Collaborate with the NUR 440 course instructor to plan and facilitate 5 applied practice-based simulation labs and 2 virtual debrief sessions, in alignment with the course theoretical concepts.  
7. Monitor student performance and assess students’ progress meeting the clinical practice expectations for the course.   
8. Foster reflection and discussion about clinical learning among students during debriefs of shadow shifts. 
9. Participate in weekly email communication with Course Faculty and provide a brief update and / or identify any concerns about students’ experiences and clinical progress.  
10. Ensure ongoing communication with students and course faculty, and clinical placement sites (as needed).  
11. Provide students with ongoing verbal feedback about their progress in meeting the clinical expectations for the course. 
12. Collaborate with course faculty and the Clinical Education Office throughout the term as needed to navigate any issues related to clinical placement activities. 
13. Complete online written midterm and final clinical evaluations of each student incorporating feedback from all clinical activities that highlight their learning and progress in meeting the clinical practice expectations.   

14. Arrange and facilitate a short 1:1 virtual meeting to review each students’ midterm and final evaluation per faculty deadlines.
